reasoning: The disagreement stems entirely from API errors (HTTP 400) in the qwen model when reviewing ums.desktop and ums.timer, not from security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 5 files and found them to be standard packaging artifacts: a typical PKGBUILD fetching pinned upstream binaries from GitHub with SHA256 checksums, standard systemd service/timer units, a desktop entry file, and .SRCINFO metadata. No malicious code, no execution of fetched content, no suspicious network operations, and no injection patterns were detected in any file.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit ums.desktop and ums.timer, forcing an 'inconclusive' verdict. The deepseek model reviewed the same files without error and found them safe. This is a tool failure, not a genuine security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review ums.desktop and ums.timer due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to security uncertainty' and 'inconclusive due to tool/API errors' in the verdict logic. API failures should be reported as coverage issues, not as security inconclusiveness.
Implement retry logic or fallback models when LLM API calls fail with transient errors (HTTP 400/500) to prevent incomplete audits from blocking verdicts.
When one model completes full coverage and finds no issues, and the other model's gaps are purely due to tool errors (not security findings), the complete audit should take precedence.
